Avery: Heads up — noticed a weird P95 jump for /chat/generate after last night's kernel-selector tweak. overall qps steady but tail latency up ~18%. :thinking_face:
Jun: repro steps? is this across all routes or a single customer route?
Avery: single high-throughput route (prod: route_id=chat/generate). the per-route dashboard shows P50 ~ unchanged, P95 up, P99 sporadic.
Lena: any correlation with seq length distribution or KV cache miss rate?
Avery: good call. dug into token-level breakdown. first-token TTFT spiked (token index 0..3). decode time per-token unchanged for later tokens, but kernel_time attribution for the first tokens jumped.
Samir: can you paste the token-level sample from the profiler? paste a tiny snippet.
Avery: sure — saved sample from profiler (sanitized):
```
[prof-sample 2155551234] route=chat/generate seq_len=48 kv_hit=false
token_idx=0 ttft_ms=72 decode_ms=9 kernel_selector=microkernel kernel_ms=58
token_idx=1 ttft_ms=18 decode_ms=6 kernel_selector=microkernel kernel_ms=10
token_idx=2 ttft_ms=19 decode_ms=6 kernel_selector=microkernel kernel_ms=11
```

Jun: wow kernel_ms 58 on token0. That's a warmup/initialization cost — looks like microkernel path is paying an init penalty for first token when KV cache is cold.
Lena: our kernel-selection heuristic recently prioritized microkernel for short seqs to save steady-state latency. We probably didn't account for per-request cold-cache kernel init.
Samir: so TTFT is dominated by kernel init for cold requests; need to separate attribution: kernel_init vs kernel_steady. can we add tags in the profiler?
Avery: proposal: add a boolean tag kernel_init=true for first token if kernel_ms > X and kv_hit=false. also emit kernel_variant label (microkernel / macro / fallback) per token in traces.
Jun: agree. also instrument per-route histogram for "first-token kernel_init_ms" and a KV-miss conditional metric. that will let us correlate P95 spikes with cold-KV patterns.
Lena: quick experiment: rollout a change to avoid selecting microkernel for requests where kv_hit is likely false (e.g., new sessions). that should reduce first-token penalty.
Samir: how do we detect "likely false" cheaply? sampling first request or look at route-level recent kv_hit_rate?
Avery: we have recent_kv_hit_rate per route in the console. simple heuristic: if route_recent_kv_hit_rate < 0.6 and seq_len < 64, prefer macro kernel that has lower init overhead.
Jun: can we add an A/B flag to try for a subset of traffic and compare token-level metrics?
Lena: yes — create rollout: 5% traffic use heuristic-v2, 95% baseline. collect kernel_init_ms, per-token kernel_variant, ttft per-token, and kv_hit boolean.
perf-bot: profiler snapshot created: https://internal.perf/shot/2155551234 — includes token attribution and kernel labels (sampled).
Samir: next actions: (1) Avery add kernel_init tag + kernel_variant to token traces (2) Jun add histograms to dashboard with kv_hit filter and first-token kernel_init_ms metric (3) Lena prepare rollout flag and traffic split (4) Samir will coordinate sampling retention for 24h.
Avery: I'm on (1) — will push a small change to tracer to emit kernel_variant and kernel_init boolean. PR later today.
Jun: I'll add dashboard panels: heatmap of first-token kernel_ms by route and kv_hit filter + timeseries for route_recent_kv_hit_rate.
Lena: I'll wire the rollout with feature-flag and a canary check — will schedule 5% for 2h then evaluate.
Samir: leave an oncall note in case P95 regresses further during rollout.
Avery: thanks. Also: suggest adding a periodic sampling job that captures token-level attribution for 1k requests per minute for important routes — avoids depending on full traces.
Jun: agreed. sampling job would be cheaper than full traces and sufficient for signal.
Lena: will sync on retro if this uncovers other kernel warmup cases (quantized kernels might behave differently).
Avery: cool — logging the thread here for visibility. ping me if you want the raw profiler export. :mag_right:
